messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: Elevated p99 tail latency + streaming stalls observed across east-west egress (us-east zones). SLO breach triggered for streaming endpoints. Affected customers: 2 enterprise customers on Dedicated pools. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.example/alerts/2495012345 (auto-generated). Please @oncall respond and triage.

maya: acked, I'm on it. marking as high priority, will grab net traces and check NAT metrics. tagging @jas for network.

eathan: quick Q — is this only streaming (server-sent event) paths or includes non-streaming generation?

maya: streaming first, but p95/p99 for non-streaming are creeping too. short snapshot from the live dashboard:
```
region: us-east-1 -> us-east-2 crosszone
streaming.p95: baseline 180ms -> 1.2s
streaming.p99: baseline 420ms -> 7.1s
nonstream.p95: 210ms -> 480ms
errors: tls_handshake_failures + 502s rising
```

jas: seeing SYN retransmits and TLS handshake timeouts between AZ-b and AZ-c on our crosszone NAT path. Also some DNS timeouts for the nat-egress proxies. Flow logs show packet drops at the egress NAT instances. (reacts :eyes:)

priya: can you paste the NAT ephemeral port metrics and conntrack? I suspect SNAT port exhaustion or conntrack backpressure.

jas: grabbing metrics...
```
metric: nat-ephemeral-ports-in-use
az-b: 63400/65535
az-c: 65280/65535
conntrack: table_usage 91% -> 99%
packet_drops: spikes on 2024-09-21T15:34:xx
```

netops-bot: automated note — detected high retransmit ratio on path az-b -> az-c, tagging netops team and opening routing probe ticket NET-8732.

sam: if conntrack / SNAT port exhaustion is real we should: 1) enable egress path failover to backup NAT in az-a, 2) scale NAT pool (spin spare gateway), 3) temporarily throttle long-running streaming sessions or convert to chunked non-streaming responses for heavy customers. I'm leaning to route failover + throttle as fastest.

maya: I'm going to flip route failover for affected subnets to the backup NAT and scale the nat pool. applying now.
```
# apply route failover
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0abc123 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --network-interface-id eni-backup-nat
# scale autoscaling group for nat-gw
aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name nat-gw-asg --desired-capacity 3
```

incident-bot: oncall handoff: maya -> sam in 15m (auto reminder).

priya: also run a small tcpdump on the affected NAT instance to confirm retransmits vs drops. maya can you grab 30s of captures and share?

maya: capture attached (sanitized) — here's the grep of retransmits:
```
15:34:02.123 IP az-b-nat > az-c-host: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
15:34:02.223 IP az-b-nat > az-c-host: Flags [S], seq 12345, (retransmit)
15:34:02.423 IP az-b-nat > az-c-host: Flags [S], seq 12345, (retransmit)
... many retransmits then RST from az-c-host
```

jas: confirmed. also DNS hits to our resolver from the NAT instances show timeouts and SERVFAIL spikes — clients retry which amplifies connections.

netops-bot: routing probe results: path MTU ok, but queuing delay spike on the az-b->az-c transit link during 15:33-15:36. Potential queueing/backpressure. Ticket NET-8732 updated.

sam: immediate mitigation checklist — marking what we did/doing: 1) Route failover to backup NAT (maya) 2) Scale nat pool to +1 instance (maya) 3) Enable conntrack-eviction experimental policy on NATs (sam) 4) Apply short-term throttling for streaming-heavy customers (priya) 5) Open long-term follow-ups for crosszone egress capacity and DNS resolver redundancy.

maya: applied route failover and scaled nat-gw-asg to 3, conntrack eviction toggle turned on on the cluster NATs. rolling restart of nat-proxy pods to pick up config.

priya: pushing feature-flag to force non-streaming fallback for two affected customers (client IDs redacted) — this reduces open long-lived connections. curl to flip flag:
```
curl -X POST https://flags.redwood.example/flip -d '{"customer":"CUST-42","flag":"streaming_fallback","value":true}'
```

maya: after the failover + scale, telemetry shows improvement:
```
post-mitigation snapshot (15:40):
streaming.p95 -> 320ms
streaming.p99 -> 1.1s
conntrack usage -> 64%
nat-ephemeral-ports az-c -> 42100
packet_drops -> near 0 after 15:36
```

jas: still seeing some TLS handshake timeouts in the tail, might be due to clients still retrying or cached DNS entries pointing to older egress IPs. DNS TTL out-of-sync suspected. We'll flush caches and nudge resolver TTLs lower.

sam: good work. real-time customer impact: both customers reported degraded streaming sessions but no complete data loss. We've notified CSM and assigned targeted mitigation for them. Need to run post-incident root-cause to fix cross-zone capacity and make NAT ephemeral scaling more graceful.

priya: follow-ups assigned: 1) netops to increase NAT autoscale headroom & add warm spare (jas) 2) infra to add connection-eviction rules and adaptive conntrack tuning (sam) 3) devexp to add streaming fallback feature for high-latency cases (ethan) 4) ops to validate DNS resolver redundancy during cross-zone failover (maya).

maya: will create incidentbridges and postmortem doc. linking runbook we used: https://wiki.redwood.example/runbooks/egress-nat-failover.

incident-bot: incident status -> mitigated. SLOs re-evaluating. Retain thread for postmortem notes & action items. (reacts :white_check_mark:)

priya: adding notes — please attach metrics export and tcpdump excerpt to the postmortem. I'll own the timeline and severity assessment.

sam: closing loop — monitoring team to keep alert escalation window open for 2 hours, then will move to P2 follow-up. thanks all. :thumbsup:
